title: Marcel On The Train by Marshall Pailet and Ethan Slater at Classic St...
transcript: Did you know that Bip The Clown was not just a mime, but a hero during the Holocaust? This new play starring Ethan Slater, who's also a co-writer on it, is about the world famous performer Marcel Marceau. Prior to becoming a famous mime, he helped Jewish children escape occupied France, and this play focuses on one such escape in 1943. Marcel and four 12-year-olds are riding a train toward Switzerland, pretending to be Boy Scouts and carrying falsified identification. It's a riveting premise, and there's just the right number of characters to enable captivating ensemble work and display an array of human responses to a time of great crisis and fear. Ethan Slater is great — he carries both humor and sorrow with ease and has clearly put in a lot of work to physicalize Marcel effectively. I felt the range he displayed in his performance was reflective of the lengths that Marcel goes to protect these kids, physically and emotionally. And on a higher level, the production's heavy subject matter is well tied with a somewhat whimsical aesthetic, illustrating the vitality of imagination and creativity even in a dire situation. I think the only thing holding this play back from good to great is its pacing, which especially sags in the second half. It's a hundred minutes but feels a little longer, and it passes over multiple obvious conclusion points, wrapping up loose ends at the cost of its momentum. Nevertheless, I thought this was a ride worth taking. With that, another program for my collection.
